newsitem.title: THAILAND: World Bank says offered Thais $1.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says offered Thais $1.5 billion.

text.p: The World Bank has offered Thailand $1.5 billion in aid as part of an international funding package to prop up the country's flagging economy, the bank's local office said.

"At the Tokyo meeting the World Bank pledged $1.5 billion of support focused on improving Thailand's competitiveness and prompting structural reforms in the economy," it said in a statement received here on Sunday.
The bank will mount a mission in September to draw up a structural adjustment program for Thailand, it added.

"Discussions held with Thai officials have resulted in the identification of areas of concentration, which includes the financial and banking sector, export promotion, labour productivity and social safety nets," it added.
The contribution brings existing pledges from donors under an International Monetary Fund-sponsored rescue package to $16.7 billion.
The money is needed to help support the Thai economy as it faces its severest crisis for decades.

Slowing economic growth last year, a slump in exports, investment in unproductive sectors and recent currency instability have eroded investor confidence in an economy which had become heavily reliant on foreign investment.
